answer: In an agent economy selling voyage plans, plume forecasts, and nectar yield estimates, voting power can be proportional to tokens locked in escrow, not account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence. To gain more control, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens for the full voting period, tying up capital and bearing its price risk rather than multiplying power with free identities.
